normal.title: Normal Boot (Clean Single OS)
normal.description: Install Ubuntu as your sole primary operating system directly on bare metal hardware for maximum performance, battery efficiency, and responsiveness.

steps.title: Download Official Ubuntu ISO Image
steps.desc: Acquire the latest official 64-bit desktop ISO release for Ubuntu. Ensure the downloaded file matches official release integrity checksums.
steps.cmdLabel: Verify SHA256 Checksum (Linux/macOS Terminal):
steps.tip: Always download Linux ISOs from official mirrors or torrents to verify cryptographic authenticity.
steps.imageCaption: Select and download official 64-bit desktop ISO release for Ubuntu

steps.title: Create a Bootable USB Flash Drive
steps.desc: Flash the downloaded ISO onto a USB flash drive (minimum 8 GB). All existing data on this USB stick will be erased.
steps.cmd: sudo dd if=ubuntu-latest.iso of=/dev/sdX bs=4M status=progress conv=fsync
steps.cmdLabel: Alternative Linux Terminal Flash (Replace /dev/sdX with USB path):
steps.warning: Double-check your target USB device path with "lsblk". Writing to the wrong disk identifier will permanently overwrite your data!
steps.imageCaption: BalenaEtcher: Select target USB drive and flash bootable installation media

steps.title: Boot into UEFI / BIOS Setup
steps.desc: Insert the bootable USB into your computer and turn it on while repeatedly tapping your motherboard boot menu key.
steps.tip: In your motherboard BIOS: Ensure UEFI Boot Mode is active and disable Fast Boot so the USB drive is promptly detected.
steps.imageCaption: Motherboard UEFI Boot Menu: Select USB flash drive as primary boot target

steps.title: Run Guided Installer & Partition Disk
steps.desc: Boot into the live desktop environment and click "Install Ubuntu". Proceed through language, keyboard layout, and timezone configuration.

options.label: Erase disk and install Ubuntu
options.detail: Recommended for clean installs: automatically creates EFI system partition, root (/), and swap space.

options.label: Encrypt new installation (LUKS)
options.detail: Optional: Secures full-disk encryption with a boot passphrase for enterprise-level privacy.

steps.tip: Provide your user account name and administrator (sudo) password when prompted, then proceed with the installation.
steps.imageCaption: Graphical Installer: Guided installation and automatic disk partitioning wizard

steps.title: Reboot & Perform First System Update
steps.desc: When installation completes, click "Restart Now" and remove the USB drive when prompted. Log into your new desktop and update package repositories.
steps.cmd: sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade -y
steps.cmdLabel: Run First System Update in Terminal:
steps.tip: Congratulations! Ubuntu is now installed as your primary operating system. Enjoy full hardware acceleration and freedom!
steps.imageCaption: First Desktop Boot: System package updater fetching security and stability updates

dual.title: Dual Boot (Windows 10/11 + Linux)
dual.description: Run Ubuntu side-by-side with your existing Windows installation on the same computer. Select which operating system to start every time you power on via the GRUB boot menu.

steps.title: Shrink Partition in Windows Disk Management
steps.desc: Boot into Windows and carve out unpartitioned space on your hard drive or SSD for Linux.
substeps: Press Win + X and select "Disk Management" (or press Win + R and type "diskmgmt.msc").
Right-click your main Windows partition (usually C:) and select "Shrink Volume...".
Enter the amount of space to shrink: enter at least 40000 MB (40 GB) up to 100000 MB (100 GB).
Click "Shrink". Crucial: Leave this newly created space as "Unallocated" — do NOT format it as NTFS in Windows!
steps.warning: Always create a backup of your personal Windows files before shrinking or modifying storage partitions.
steps.imageCaption: Windows Disk Management: Inspect drive partitions and shrink C: volume to create Unallocated Space

steps.title: Disable Windows Fast Startup & BitLocker
steps.desc: Windows Fast Startup puts system disks into a locked hibernation cache that blocks Linux from safely reading partitions or installing the GRUB bootloader.
substeps: Open Control Panel → Hardware and Sound → Power Options → "Choose what the power buttons do".
Click "Change settings that are currently unavailable".
Uncheck "Turn on fast startup (recommended)" and click Save Changes.
If BitLocker encryption is active on drive C:, suspend BitLocker in Windows settings and keep your 48-digit recovery key accessible.
steps.warning: Failing to turn off Fast Startup may lead to read-only disk mounts or filesystem conflicts when switching between operating systems.
steps.imageCaption: Windows Power Options: Uncheck "Turn on fast startup" to avoid partition hibernation lock

steps.title: Flash USB with Rufus (UEFI / GPT)
steps.desc: Flash Ubuntu ISO using Rufus with the correct partition scheme for modern UEFI machines.
substeps: Open Rufus on Windows and select your USB flash drive.
Choose the downloaded ISO file.
Partition scheme: Select "GPT".
Target system: Select "UEFI (non-CSM)".
Click Start to write the image.
steps.tip: In your PC BIOS setup: Ensure the SATA controller mode is set to AHCI (not Intel RST or RAID mode).
steps.imageCaption: Rufus: Select Partition scheme "GPT" and Target system "UEFI (non-CSM)"

steps.title: Install Ubuntu Alongside Windows
steps.desc: Boot from your USB flash drive and launch the graphical installer.
substeps: When reaching the Installation Type step, select: "Install Ubuntu alongside Windows Boot Manager" (recommended automatic mode).
If choosing Manual Partitioning ("Something else"): Select the Free Unallocated Space, create an EFI partition (if needed), and a Root (/) partition formatted as ext4 or btrfs.
Ensure the bootloader is placed on the primary disk EFI partition (e.g., /dev/nvme0n1 or /dev/sda).
steps.tip: The installer will automatically detect Windows Boot Manager and add an entry into the GRUB bootloader.
steps.imageCaption: Installer Type: Select "Install alongside Windows Boot Manager" for automatic dual-boot config

steps.title: Reboot & Select OS via GRUB Menu
steps.desc: Remove the USB flash drive and restart your PC. The GRUB bootloader menu will now appear on startup, letting you select Linux or Windows.
steps.cmd: sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade -y
steps.cmdLabel: Initial Update Command in Linux:
steps.tip: If your computer boots straight into Windows, enter BIOS/UEFI settings and move the Linux GRUB entry to the top of your Boot Priority list.
steps.imageCaption: GNU GRUB Bootloader: Switch seamlessly between Linux and Windows Boot Manager

vm.title: Virtual Machine (Safe Sandbox)
vm.description: Run Ubuntu safely inside an isolated virtual window on your current Windows, macOS, or Linux desktop without modifying your physical storage drives or bootloader.

steps.title: Install a Virtualization Hypervisor
steps.desc: Install hypervisor software suited for your host operating system.
tools: Oracle VirtualBox (Free & Open Source for Windows, Mac, Linux)
UTM (Native high-performance hypervisor for Apple Silicon Mac M1/M2/M3)
steps.tip: Ensure CPU Virtualization (Intel VT-x or AMD-V) is enabled in your BIOS/UEFI settings.
steps.imageCaption: Oracle VM VirtualBox: Open-source hypervisor manager for running isolated virtual machines

steps.title: Create a New Virtual Machine Profile
steps.desc: Open your hypervisor and click "New" to allocate virtual hardware resources for Ubuntu.
substeps: Name: "Ubuntu VM"
Type: Linux | Version: Debian (64-bit)
Base Memory (RAM): Allocate at least 4096 MB (4 GB). If your host has 16GB+ RAM, assign 6GB-8GB.
Processors: Assign 2 to 4 virtual CPU cores for responsive graphics and app loading.
Virtual Hard Disk: Create a 25 GB to 40 GB dynamically allocated disk (VDI or VMDK format).
steps.imageCaption: Virtual Machine Creation Wizard: Allocate base memory RAM and virtual CPU processor cores

steps.title: Attach ISO & Enable Video Acceleration
steps.desc: Mount the downloaded ISO into the virtual machine optical disc drive and optimize display parameters.
substeps: Go to VM Settings → Storage → Optical Drive → Choose a disk file → select the downloaded ISO.
Go to VM Settings → Display → Increase Video Memory to 128 MB.
Check "Enable 3D Acceleration" (ensures smooth window compositing and desktop animations).
steps.imageCaption: Storage Settings: Mount downloaded Linux ISO to Virtual Optical Drive and allocate video memory

steps.title: Power On & Complete In-Window Setup
steps.desc: Click "Start" to launch the virtual machine. The installer runs safely isolated inside your application window.
substeps: Select "Try or Install" in the virtual boot menu.
Choose "Erase disk and install" — this only touches the virtual disk (.vdi), NOT your physical computer!
Complete username, password, and desktop layout setup, then restart the virtual machine.
steps.tip: In VirtualBox, press the Right Control key (Host Key) anytime if your mouse cursor gets trapped inside the VM window.
steps.imageCaption: Live Installer executing safely inside virtual window without altering host disk partitions

steps.title: Install Guest Additions for Seamless Display
steps.desc: Install hypervisor integration tools to enable automatic window resolution scaling, bidirectional clipboard, and folder sharing.
steps.cmd: sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y virtualbox-guest-x11
steps.cmdLabel: Run Inside VM Terminal to Enable Guest Features:
substeps: In VirtualBox top menu: Click Devices → "Insert Guest Additions CD image...".
Run the terminal command above to install native kernel integration packages.
Reboot the virtual machine to enjoy auto-resizing full-screen resolution and shared clipboard!
steps.imageCaption: VirtualBox Guest Additions: Dynamic window resolution auto-fit, clipboard sharing and folders

dual.title: Dual Boot (Windows 10/11 + Linux)

steps.title: Shrink Partition in Windows Disk Management
steps.desc: Boot into Windows and carve out unpartitioned space on your hard drive or SSD for Linux.
substeps: Press Win + X and select "Disk Management" (or press Win + R and type "diskmgmt.msc").
Right-click your main Windows partition (usually C:) and select "Shrink Volume...".
Enter the amount of space to shrink: enter at least 40000 MB (40 GB) up to 100000 MB (100 GB).
Click "Shrink". Crucial: Leave this newly created space as "Unallocated" — do NOT format it as NTFS in Windows!
steps.warning: Always create a backup of your personal Windows files before shrinking or modifying storage partitions.
steps.imageCaption: Windows Disk Management: Inspect drive partitions and shrink C: volume to create Unallocated Space

steps.title: Disable Windows Fast Startup & BitLocker
steps.desc: Windows Fast Startup puts system disks into a locked hibernation cache that blocks Linux from safely reading partitions or installing the GRUB bootloader.
substeps: Open Control Panel → Hardware and Sound → Power Options → "Choose what the power buttons do".
Click "Change settings that are currently unavailable".
Uncheck "Turn on fast startup (recommended)" and click Save Changes.
If BitLocker encryption is active on drive C:, suspend BitLocker in Windows settings and keep your 48-digit recovery key accessible.
steps.warning: Failing to turn off Fast Startup may lead to read-only disk mounts or filesystem conflicts when switching between operating systems.
steps.imageCaption: Windows Power Options: Uncheck "Turn on fast startup" to avoid partition hibernation lock

steps.title: Create a New Virtual Machine Profile

steps.title: Attach ISO & Enable Video Acceleration
steps.desc: Mount the downloaded ISO into the virtual machine optical disc drive and optimize display parameters.

Check "Enable 3D Acceleration" (ensures smooth window compositing and desktop animations).

steps.title: Power On & Complete In-Window Setup

Complete username, password, and desktop layout setup, then restart the virtual machine.

steps.imageCaption: Live Installer executing safely inside virtual window without altering host disk partitions

steps.cmdLabel: Run Inside VM Terminal to Enable Guest Features:

Reboot the virtual machine to enjoy auto-resizing full-screen resolution and shared clipboard!

steps.title: Shrink Partition in Windows Disk Management
steps.desc: Boot into Windows and carve out unpartitioned space on your hard drive or SSD for Linux.
substeps: Press Win + X and select "Disk Management" (or press Win + R and type "diskmgmt.msc").
Right-click your main Windows partition (usually C:) and select "Shrink Volume...".
Enter the amount of space to shrink: enter at least 40000 MB (40 GB) up to 100000 MB (100 GB).
Click "Shrink". Crucial: Leave this newly created space as "Unallocated" — do NOT format it as NTFS in Windows!
steps.warning: Always create a backup of your personal Windows files before shrinking or modifying storage partitions.
steps.imageCaption: Windows Disk Management: Inspect drive partitions and shrink C: volume to create Unallocated Space

steps.title: Disable Windows Fast Startup & BitLocker
steps.desc: Windows Fast Startup puts system disks into a locked hibernation cache that blocks Linux from safely reading partitions or installing the GRUB bootloader.
substeps: Open Control Panel → Hardware and Sound → Power Options → "Choose what the power buttons do".
Click "Change settings that are currently unavailable".
Uncheck "Turn on fast startup (recommended)" and click Save Changes.
If BitLocker encryption is active on drive C:, suspend BitLocker in Windows settings and keep your 48-digit recovery key accessible.
steps.warning: Failing to turn off Fast Startup may lead to read-only disk mounts or filesystem conflicts when switching between operating systems.

substeps: Open Control Panel → Hardware and Sound → Power Options → "Choose what the power buttons do".
Click "Change settings that are currently unavailable".
Uncheck "Turn on fast startup (recommended)" and click Save Changes.
If BitLocker encryption is active on drive C:, suspend BitLocker in Windows settings and keep your 48-digit recovery key accessible.
steps.warning: Failing to turn off Fast Startup may lead to read-only disk mounts or filesystem conflicts when switching between operating systems.
steps.imageCaption: Windows Power Options: Uncheck "Turn on fast startup" to avoid partition hibernation lock

steps.title: Flash USB with Rufus (UEFI / GPT)
steps.desc: Flash Zorin OS ISO using Rufus with the correct partition scheme for modern UEFI machines.
substeps: Open Rufus on Windows and select your USB flash drive.
Choose the downloaded ISO file.
Partition scheme: Select "GPT".
Target system: Select "UEFI (non-CSM)".
Click Start to write the image.
steps.tip: In your PC BIOS setup: Ensure the SATA controller mode is set to AHCI (not Intel RST or RAID mode).
steps.imageCaption: Rufus: Select Partition scheme "GPT" and Target system "UEFI (non-CSM)"

steps.title: Install Zorin OS Alongside Windows
steps.desc: Boot from your USB flash drive and launch the graphical installer.
substeps: When reaching the Installation Type step, select: "Install Zorin OS alongside Windows Boot Manager" (recommended automatic mode).
If choosing Manual Partitioning ("Something else"): Select the Free Unallocated Space, create an EFI partition (if needed), and a Root (/) partition formatted as ext4 or btrfs.
Ensure the bootloader is placed on the primary disk EFI partition (e.g., /dev/nvme0n1 or /dev/sda).
steps.tip: The installer will automatically detect Windows Boot Manager and add an entry into the GRUB bootloader.
steps.imageCaption: Installer Type: Select "Install alongside Windows Boot Manager" for automatic dual-boot config

steps.title: Reboot & Select OS via GRUB Menu
steps.desc: Remove the USB flash drive and restart your PC. The GRUB bootloader menu will now appear on startup, letting you select Linux or Windows.

name: Void Linux
tagline: General purpose operating system from scratch
description: Void Linux is an independent, rolling-release distribution built from scratch rather than being a fork. keyFeatures: Proprietary XBPS package manager engineered in C for blistering performance

steps.desc: Boot into Windows and carve out unpartitioned space on your hard drive or SSD for Linux.
substeps: Press Win + X and select "Disk Management" (or press Win + R and type "diskmgmt.msc").
Right-click your main Windows partition (usually C:) and select "Shrink Volume...".

Click "Shrink". Crucial: Leave this newly created space as "Unallocated" — do NOT format it as NTFS in Windows!

steps.title: Disable Windows Fast Startup & BitLocker
steps.desc: Windows Fast Startup puts system disks into a locked hibernation cache that blocks Linux from safely reading partitions or installing the GRUB bootloader.
substeps: Open Control Panel → Hardware and Sound → Power Options → "Choose what the power buttons do".
Click "Change settings that are currently unavailable".
Uncheck "Turn on fast startup (recommended)" and click Save Changes.

steps.warning: Failing to turn off Fast Startup may lead to read-only disk mounts or filesystem conflicts when switching between operating systems.
